title: An optogenetics device with smartphone video capture to introduce neurotechnology and systems neuroscience to high school students.
quote: We found that only flies that expressed CsChrimson in the GF and had been fed retinal displayed takeoff behaviors (Fig 2B and S1 Movie).
mapping_basis: Paper states the GF is 'also known in the literature as DNp01'; synonyms.csv maps GF/Giant Fiber to DNp01.
stimulation: 627 nm red LED, 300 ms, 0.16 mW/mm2 at the fly, 2 mm from LED
sensory_condition: tethered to tungsten wire under stereoscope, holding a piece of Kimwipe
coordination_notes: escape consists of a rapid, synchronized middle leg extension, wing depression and flight initiation
penetrance: ~84% of GF x CsChrimson + flies escaped (Fig 2B)
n_flies_note: n = 24 per genotype as printed in Fig 2B
notes: Single take-off movement (leg extension), not rhythmic stepping; legs coded 'no' per PROTOCOL section 3. Flies were tethered, so no walking surface; walking not assessed.

title: An optogenetics device with smartphone video capture to introduce neurotechnology and systems neuroscience to high school students.
quote: We found that flies expressing CsChrimson in neurons labeled by this line displayed freezing behavior at a high probability (Fig 3A, 3B and S2 Movie).
mapping_basis: Line SS1540 (VT023490-p65AD; R38F04-GAL4DBD) is listed in driver_lines.csv as AMBIGUOUS with candidates DNp09;DNp71, preferred/name-as-written DNp09; the paper names DNp09 for this line.
stimulation: 627 nm red LED, 300 ms, 0.16 mW/mm2 at the fly, 2 mm from LED
sensory_condition: tethered to tungsten wire under stereoscope, no tarsal contact
other_cell_types: other unidentified neurons labelled by SS1540-split-Gal4 proposed to drive freezing
coordination_notes: complete interruption of appendage movement during and after stimulation
penetrance: ~62% freezing in SS1540 x CsChrimson + flies (Fig 3B)
n_flies_note: n = 80 retinal-fed flies as printed in Fig 3B
notes: Paper notes freezing was initially attributed to DNp09 but may be due to other neurons in this line, and that the DNp09 locomotion increase was not observed here ('we did not observe the other reported behavioral output of this line, an increase in locomotion driven by DNp09'), attributed to the tethered preparation lacking tarsal contact. Freezing coded 'no' for all leg pairs per PROTOCOL section 3.

title: Cell body clustering drives gap junction-mediated synchronous activity in command neurons
source_locator: Results, 'Hunchback is required in MDNs for backward walking'; Fig. 1C (control)
quote: In control animals, when adult MDNs are optogenetically activated, the animals walk backwards (Fig. 1C)
mapping_basis: Paper's 'Moonwalker Descending Neuron (MDN)' is the MANC type MDN in type_list.csv; driver is MDN-Gal4 (VT50600.p65AD; VT44845.Gal4DBD, SS03131).
stimulation: 627 nm red LED from above, 5 s per trial, >=10 s inter-trial interval
sensory_condition: individual fly in a 1 mL serological pipette, 22-25 C, reared on all-trans retinal
coordination_notes: paper describes backward walking initiation as brief bilateral hindleg flexion then bilateral power stroke before alternating leg movements
n_flies_note: Fig. 1C shows ~13 control data points; exact n not stated in text
notes: Control (UAS-Luc RNAi) genotype of the Hb-knockdown experiment; the same control MDN activation is repeated in Fig. 2K and Fig. 3M ('Control animals walked backward when MDN was optogenetically activated'). Backward walking coded 'yes' for all three leg pairs per PROTOCOL section 3. Knockdown conditions (Hb, Lar, Inx8 RNAi) are perturbations of MDN rather than clean activations: there activation failed to elicit backward locomotion or caused pausing; not recorded separately.
